claim.claim: The increase in Tesla's operating expenses in 2025 was driven primarily by AI-related research and development.

verdict.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: R&D expense increased $1.87 billion, or 41%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs

R&D expenses increased $1.36 billion, or 42%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2025 as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2024. These increases were primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs
SG&A expenses increased $684 million, or 13%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024

verdict.reasoning_summary: The claim states that the increase in Tesla's operating expenses in 2025 was driven primarily by AI-related research and development. Operating expenses consist of R&D and SG&A expenses. Evidence E2 shows R&D expense increased $1.87 billion (41%) in 2025 vs 2024, "primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs." Evidence E5 shows SG&A increased $684 million (13%) in the same period. The R&D increase ($1.87B) is significantly larger than the SG&A increase ($684M), and the filing explicitly attributes the R&D increase primarily to AI-related costs. This supports the claim that AI-related R&D was the primary driver of the overall operating expense increase. Evidence E4 provides corroborating information for the nine-month period showing the same pattern and attribution to AI.
